text: If the placenta hasn't come away 24 hours after birth, it starts to smell strongly and the risk of uterine infection rises. At the 24-hour mark, remove as much of the membrane as possible — gentle, steady tension on the membranes often lets it detach without damage. Antibiotics are recommended, either by injection or as boluses placed directly in the uterus right after the placenta is removed. Injecting prostaglandin (Lutalyse), with a booster 15 days later, helps ensure the uterus is fully cleared and ready for a new pregnancy.
